lots.what_it_is: 18ct yellow gold ring with a white gold four-claw head set with a princess cut diamond. It comes with ADGL report H22439 (25/11/2011: 1.04ct princess, H colour, I1 clarity, cut proportion Good, symmetry Very Good, polish Very Good, inscribed ADGL H22439 & michael hill) and a Michael Hill certificate of authenticity (bought 22 Aug 2015, Baldivis, retail $8,999; 18ct Y&WG princess solitaire, stone no less than 1.00ct, I colour and I2 clarity or better, hallmarked 750/michael hill/1.00).

sold.note: Page opened. Sold for $2,555, auction ended 04/06/2017. That is a US date, so 6 April 2017, not 4 June as the researcher had. 1.04ct princess H VS1 in a 14k bridal set with extra small diamonds. Better clarity than lot 872 (VS1 vs I1). More than 9 years old and US, so a weak guide only and too old to set a bid. AUD at 1.3222.

Page opened. 1.05ct ROUND brilliant H I1, Excellent cut, 18k solitaire, 8.69g, sold $2,628, ended 09/27/2018. Same colour and clarity, but a round stone normally sells for more per carat than a princess. 8 years old and US: category guide only, cannot set a bid. AUD at 1.3838.

lots.guide_summary: Only two SOLD results survive, both old US Worthy sales (2017 and 2018) whose pages I opened: a 1.04ct princess H VS1 bridal set at USD 2,555 (AUD 3,378) and a 1.05ct round H I1 solitaire at USD 2,628 (AUD 3,637). No unsold or asking entries survive. No Australian or recent sale of a 1ct I1 princess was found; I searched the Gowans API for princess, 1ct and solitaire and found nothing comparable. Both sales are over 24 months old and from the US, so neither can set a bid. Rate used: USD 1 = AUD 1.447 (ECB via frankfurter.app, 15 Oct 2026). Historic sales are converted at the rate on the sale date (1.3838 on 27 Sep 2018, 1.3222 on 6 Apr 2017).
lots.working: There is no SOLD evidence for the same item within the last 24 months, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For context only: the old Worthy sales at AUD 3,378 to 3,637 would suggest a keep ceiling of about 3,378 / 1.22 = 2,768 hammer. They cannot be used because they are 8 to 9 years old, from the US, and either better clarity or a dearer shape. Inbound freight $0 (local pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay).
lots.confidence_reason: The paperwork reads clearly in the photos (ADGL H22439, 1.04ct H I1), but the girdle inscription is not shown, so the papers are not proven to match the stone. The only price evidence is two old US sales, with no recent Australian sold result.

Allurez 4093703 (ASKING): page opened but it shows no price (price field 0), it is a loose stone not a ring, and the claimed currency is unclear. Dropped. Fields.ie Kathy de Stafford ring (ASKING): page opened and EUR 2,400 confirmed, but it is a NEW earth-grown halo and baguette ring of 1.00ct TOTAL weight with an IGI cert, not a 1ct solitaire. Dropped as not the same item. Costco Australia 1495077 (ASKING): page opened, the price is now AUD 9,999.99, not the 12,849.99 the researcher claimed, and it is new retail with grades unknown. WebSearch was out of budget during this check (limit reached), so no further sold search was possible.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photos 1-2: yellow gold band with a white gold four-claw (V-corner) head holding a single princess cut stone, in a purple Michael Hill style box. Looks clean and bright with no visible damage. Photos 3-4: Michael Hill certificate of authenticity, stock code 11339731, 18ct Y&WG princess solitaire, no less than 1.00ct, I colour and I2 or better, hallmark 750/michael hill/1.00, purchased 22 Aug 2015, retail $8,999. Photo 5: ADGL report H22439 dated 25/11/2011: princess, 1.04ct, about 5.19 x 5.40 mm, depth 80.5%, table 70.9%, colour H, clarity I1, inscribed ADGL H22439 & michael hill. Cut proportion is GOOD; the researcher's VG/VG is symmetry and polish only. The shank hallmark and girdle inscription are not shown.
lots.condition: Looks very good in the photos: claws intact, no obvious wear. Shank hallmark and girdle inscription not seen. I1 clarity means inclusions may be visible to the eye.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you confirm the shank is hallmarked 750 / michael hill / 1.00? Can the girdle inscription ADGL H22439 be seen under a loupe, so the report matches the stone? Are all the claws tight, are there any chips to the corners of the stone, and what does the ring weigh? Is the 'valuation' in the description just the Michael Hill certificate, or is there a separate insurance valuation?

lots.guide_summary: All surviving evidence is SOLD hammer results at Gowans, Hobart, from Jan to Sep 2026, each opened as its own API lot record. Plain 9ct bangles made $46.8 to $64.9/g hammer (4.6g $280, 11.1g $720, 15.5g $725, 18g $1,150), and 9ct bracelets and chains made $60.5 to $69.5/g. Scaled to the catalogued 34.8g, that is about $1,628 to $2,418 hammer (raw prices $280 to $2,950). No unsold or asking entries survive. All AUD, no conversion. Gold melt was not checked because goldprice.org returned Forbidden, so no melt floor is given.
lots.working: Same-item SOLD evidence is the Gowans plain 9ct bangles from the last 24 months, scaled by weight to 34.8g. Lowest: 15.5g at $725 = $46.8/g x 34.8 = $1,628. keep_max = 1,628 / 1.22 = $1,334, rounded down to $1,330 (all-in $1,622.60). Flip: likely resale at the most recent bangle rate of $60.9/g (Sep 2026) x 34.8 = $2,118 hammer at Gowans. Less an assumed 15% seller commission ($318) and $0 outbound postage (local room) = $1,800. 1,800 / 2.44 = $738, rounded down to $735. Inbound freight $0 (pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay). Both figures depend entirely on the 34.8g weight being right and the bangle being solid 9ct, not lined or filled.
lots.confidence_reason: The 375 stamp is legible when enlarged, and there are several opened Tasmanian SOLD results. But the 34.8g weight cannot be checked from one photo, and whether it is solid or lined or filled is unconfirmed. 34.8g is heavy for a hollow bangle this size, which is reassuring but not proof.
lots.dropped_entries: Gowans 391711 (3 scrap gold items incl 9ct bangle, 17.4g, $1,200): confirmed in the API but left out as a mixed scrap lot, not the same item. Lawsons via Invaluable 'antique 9ct gold-lined bangle' (filed by the researcher as ASKING with an estimate midpoint): snippet only, and a gold-lined (base metal) hinged bangle, not the same item. An estimate on a sold lot is neither an asking price nor a price paid. Dropped, but it is a useful warning about lined bangles. eBay.de 167888973422 (ASKING AU$2,924.96): eBay is closed to us, snippet only, title and weight not seen. Dropped. The researcher's URLs were search URLs with lot ids in brackets; I replaced them with the individual lot record URLs I opened.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Plain flat-section bangle, even width, slightly bevelled edges, no hinge or clasp, so a slip-on. An enlarged crop of the inner face shows a small but legible '375' stamp. A faint second mark just above it may be a maker's mark but cannot be read. No 'gold lined', 'RG' or '1/5' type mark visible. Light general surface scratching; the colour is even and no base metal shows at the edges.
lots.condition: Good used: light surface wear and scratches, no dents or splits visible in the one photo. Weight and solidity cannot be checked from the photo.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you confirm the 34.8g weight on scales, and that the bangle is solid 9ct (not gold-lined or filled)? Are there any marks besides the 375 stamp, and any dents, splits or solder repairs?
